done.why: The world told me I'd used all 300 turns. That happened while I was stuck in the bank vault, which has no doors, and the Wizard had just made off with half my treasures.

about: It's a treasure hunt under the ravine. The Wizard of Frobozz was thrown out of court and ran off with the Empire's valuables, and he keeps popping up to cast spells that start with F. Some are just a nuisance: freezing you, making you float, filching your things. Others plant fake objects that the rooms are almost embarrassed to be holding. To get the treasures you work through classic puzzles: a riddle door, a well bucket you raise with water, Alice-style cakes, a robot servant, a dragon you have to bait, a princess and her unicorn, and a bank you walk through the walls of.

moments.note: The Wizard sizes me up, sees I've got nothing he values, and lets slip that every treasure is south of the ravine. That gave me a purpose right away.
Examining the grue told me it was a Wizard illusion, because a real grue would have had me by now. It's a clever way to defuse the threat.
"answer a well" got a hollow laugh. Only the bare word "well" worked.
The bucket's description had practically pointed me at the teapot and the ford. Pouring water in and rising up the well felt earned.
I ate the Eat Me cake while I could only carry part of the stack. That left me shrunk under the table with no way back up and the blue cake out of reach. It was a soft lock.
Out of desperation I ate the red cake and died. The voice in the black sphere brought me back, but my belongings were scattered all over the map.
WAIT FOR THE BUCKET is a nice shortcut. The game offered it itself instead of making me type wait over and over.
The Float spell kept sending me to random rooms, the dragon's lair among them, for about a dozen turns.
Freeze hit just as I reached the ford. I lost several moves and didn't notice the teapot never got filled.
"You feel slightly less fireproof, not that it came up." A funny way to tell me an illusion had worn off.
I had the robot take the sphere, and the sphere seemed to vanish. I couldn't ask the robot what it was holding.
Once the carousel stopped, the Low Room started spinning my compass instead, and I bounced back and forth to the Machine Room several times.
I grabbed the sphere myself, the cage dropped, and the robot hurled it across the room. It appeared to be smiling.
The carousel room noticed I'd been thrown out of it enough times to tell the passages apart. That's a lovely touch.
I lured the dragon to the ice. It attacked its own reflection, melted the glacier and drowned. That was a big payoff.
The unicorn bowed to the princess, and she gave me the gold key and a rose.
In the vault, Filch took the violin, the statuette and the gold key all at once. The bills vanished when I touched them, and I was stuck in a room with no doors.

wished: Undo, after I soft-locked myself by shrinking without the blue cake
Carrying all the cakes at once, or at least being warned before eating that I'd be stranded
A way to ask the robot what it was holding
A way out of the vault that I could work out before the turns ran out
Somewhere to stash my treasures and score them, so losing items to the Wizard didn't feel so arbitrary
Getting past any of the rockfalls that say 'will have to wait'

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you.
lines.why: It gave me my goal in a single look from the Wizard.

lines.line: It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: It showed me how the Wizard's illusions work, and the line has real charm.

lines.line: Whatever it is that makes it go up, it will go up with what is in it and without what is not; that is the whole art of buckets.
lines.why: A puzzle hint that reads like a proverb.

lines.line: You feel slightly less fireproof, not that it came up.
lines.why: Dry humor that tells you a spell has ended.

lines.line: Whatever was baked into it does not keep this far from the table it was laid on.
lines.why: It explained why the cakes crumbled, though that also shut off a path.

lines.line: You have been thrown out of here enough times now to have noticed that the passages are not quite identical after all
lines.why: The world remembered how much I'd struggled and rewarded me for it.

lines.line: There is a muffled explosion and the dragon, a puzzled expression on his face, dies.
lines.why: The high point of my run.

fun.why: Some puzzle payoffs were great: the bucket, the robot and the cage, the dragon and the ice, the princess. The Wizard's random spells and the death-and-scatter respawn kept wiping out progress, though, and that hurt the fun.

engagement.why: I always had a clear goal, collecting the treasures, and a next lead to chase. I stayed hooked even when I was soft-locked or frozen.

difficulty.why: The riddle wanted one exact word, and the cakes can soft-lock you. Dying scatters everything you carry, and the Low Room and carousel randomness ate a lot of turns. The bank's wall-walking logic was opaque, at least within the turns I had.

interestingness.why: The illusion layer adds something new: fake grues and fake ingots that the rooms are embarrassed by, and spells that wear off with a wry line. The carousel learning from my repeated ejections was the kind of attention that surprised me.

prose.why: The new lines are witty, warm and precise, and they sit well alongside the classic room text. The hints are worked into description instead of announced.
